text:
Maria (Payroll): Quick heads up — ran into ~40 paystubs where payroll export shows NY state UI and 'New York City' local tax still applied even though these folks were working from NJ >30 days this quarter. Need retrofix and W-2 impact? :thinking:

payroll-bot: Automated check flagged 40 employees: payroll_export_202703.csv -> mismatch: work_state!=tax_state :eyes:

Jonah (People Ops): Yikes. Are these remote-week splits or full-remote relocations?

Maria (Payroll): Mix — about 28 are full-remote (per HR profile moved to NJ but paycode didn't update), 12 are week-splitting (NY office days + NJ remote days). The week-split ones are the trickiest for UI rate and local tax.

Priya (Tax Counsel): @Maria can you paste a sample row (no PII) and indicate whether we used employee's residence or work location for UI withholding? :memo:

Maria (Payroll): Here's sample (sanitized):
```
emp_id, residence_state, work_state, pay_state, ui_rate_applied, local_tax
1001,NJ,NJ,NY,4.2,NYC
1002,NJ,NY,NJ,3.8,None
```

Maria (Payroll): In some cases pay_state stayed NY due to legacy profile. Vendor says they default to 'office state' when both present. Not ideal.

Sam (HRBP): For the 28 full-remote NJ folks HR changed address in Workday in Apr. Payroll got the update but pay_state mapping didn't. We need to notify employees if we file amended returns.

Priya (Tax Counsel): For UI and SUI, employer liability is on where services performed. For full-remote NJ residents who performed all work in NJ, we need to reclassify and adjust employer UI contributions retroactively. For week-split, allocate wages by days worked per state — if >50% NJ, NJ rules. We may need W-2c for state wage boxes (box 16) and local where applicable.

Jonah (People Ops): What's the operational plan? Does payroll vendor do retro payruns and file W-2c? How long?

Maria (Payroll): Proposed plan:
1) Confirm per-employee day logs from timekeeping by Thurs noon.
2) Generate correcting journal entries and retro payruns for UI adjustments by Fri EOD.
3) Engage vendor for W-2c prep — likely 30-45 days for filing and employee copies.
4) Draft employee comms explaining changes and any net-pay impact.

Priya (Tax Counsel): Also check SUTA and SUI caps per year for NJ and NY to compute employer-side delta. If overwithheld employee tax changed, we may need to refund or apply to next payrun.

Sam (HRBP): I can pull the timecards and owner the employee comms. Will coordinate with OKRs: cc @Jonah.

Jonah (People Ops): I'll request an expedited SOW with vendor for the retrofix. Budget wise expect some vendor fees + possible state filing fees. Finance FYI: @Evan (Finance) — can we get a small commit for corrections?

Maria (Payroll): Evan FYI — rough estimate $6k vendor + $3k state fees based on prior W-2c project.

payroll-bot: New task created: #payroll-retrofix-1716004321 assigned to Maria, vendor_ticket_5821.

Evan (Finance): Acknowledged. Please paste final scope before vendor sign.

Maria (Payroll): Will report back with list of affected emp_ids and projected cash impact by tomorrow noon. Thanks team :pray:

Jonah (People Ops): Great — can we aim for employee comms draft by EOD Friday? Sam + Priya to review.

Sam (HRBP): On it. Quick Q: For week-split employees who owe small tax deltas, do we net from next paycheck or issue separate checks?

Priya (Tax Counsel): If amounts small (<$50) and employee consents, netting is permissible; otherwise issue check. State rules vary — we'll flag per-employee in the spreadsheet.

Maria (Payroll): Noted. I'll include netting suggestions column.

Jonah (People Ops): Thanks everyone. Re-open if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
